papers.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
papers.version: arXiv:1301.3781v3 (2013-09-07); listed in ICLR 2013 Workshop Proceedings
papers.notes: Reproduction target is pinned to arXiv v3 because this is the version containing Tables 1-8 and the large-scale/qualitative results used in the project.

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
papers.notes: Official NeurIPS proceedings PDF is used as the primary source.

targets.description: Reproduce/verify the stated CBOW and Skip-gram architecture: CBOW predicts the center word from surrounding context; Skip-gram predicts surrounding words from the center word.
targets.notes: Architecture target, not a numeric benchmark.

targets.description: Verify the Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test-set taxonomy: 5 semantic and 9 syntactic relation types and the representative examples.
targets.notes: The full test set is stated to contain 8,869 semantic and 10,675 syntactic questions.

targets.description: Reproduce CBOW accuracy scaling over training words [24M,49M,98M,196M,391M,783M] and dimensions [50,100,300,600], restricted to questions whose words are in the top-30K vocabulary. Reference rows: 50d=[13.4,15.7,18.6,19.1,22.5,23.2], 100d=[19.4,23.1,27.8,28.7,33.4,32.2], 300d=[23.2,29.2,35.3,38.6,43.7,45.9], 600d=[24.0,30.1,36.5,40.8,46.6,50.4].

Reproduce the 640-dimensional architecture comparison on the same 320M-word/82K-vocabulary LDC data. Reference (semantic, syntactic, MSR syntactic-relatedness): RNNLM=(9,36,35), NNLM=(23,53,47), CBOW=(24,64,61), Skip-gram=(55,59,56). RNNLM is a reported external/pre-existing baseline; the project scope directly implements NNLM, CBOW, and Skip-gram.

Reproduce the full-vocabulary analogy comparison. Project-trained rows of primary interest: Our NNLM 20d/6B=(12.9,26.4,20.3), 50d/6B=(27.9,55.8,43.2), 100d/6B=(34.2,64.5,50.8); CBOW 300d/783M=(15.5,53.1,36.1); Skip-gram 300d/783M=(50.0,55.9,53.3). External published vectors remain reference baselines.

Reproduce the epoch/data/dimension trade-off. Reference total accuracies/training times: CBOW 300d 783M 3ep=36.1/1d; SG 300d 783M 3ep=53.3/3d; CBOW 300d 783M 1ep=33.6/0.3d; CBOW 300d 1.6B 1ep=36.1/0.6d; CBOW 600d 783M 1ep=36.2/0.7d; SG 300d 783M 1ep=49.2/1d; SG 300d 1.6B 1ep=53.8/2d; SG 600d 783M 1ep=55.5/2.5d.
targets.notes: Training-time reproduction should be interpreted relative to available hardware as well as raw wall time.

targets.description: Reproduce/compare the 6B-word DistBelief large-scale results: NNLM 100d total=50.8, 14d×180 CPU cores; CBOW 1000d total=63.7, 2d×140; Skip-gram 1000d total=65.6, 2.5d×125.
targets.notes: Exact DistBelief/50-100-replica environment is unavailable; catalog records the original specification, while an execution surrogate has not yet been canonically bound.

targets.description: Reproduce the Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge result for Skip-gram and the reported combination: Skip-gram=48.0%; Skip-gram+RNNLMs=58.9% overall (59.2% dev, 58.7% test).
targets.notes: Project scope directly trains the Skip-gram component; the RNNLM combination is a reference/composite result.

targets.description: Reproduce the listed word-relation analogies using the Table-4 best Skip-gram vectors (300d, 783M words), including relation examples such as France-Paris, big-bigger, Miami-Florida, Einstein-scientist, and Microsoft-Windows.
targets.notes: The paper notes that exact-match scoring of these examples is only about 60%.

targets.description: Verify the reported claim that using ten examples instead of one to form the relation vector improves the best model by about 10 percentage points absolute on the semantic-syntactic test.
Verify the Skip-gram architecture and nearby-word prediction objective.
Reproduce the two-dimensional PCA projection of 1000-dimensional Skip-gram vectors for countries and their capital cities, preserving the qualitative parallel relationship structure.
targets.notes: The figure caption gives dimensionality but does not fully specify the training corpus/objective used for this exact plot.

targets.description: Reproduce 300d Skip-gram objective/subsampling comparison on the word analogy task. No-subsampling rows (time min, syntactic, semantic, total): NEG-5=(38,63,54,59), NEG-15=(97,63,58,61), HS-Huffman=(41,53,40,47), NCE-5=(38,60,45,53). With 1e-5 subsampling: NEG-5=(14,61,58,60), NEG-15=(36,61,61,61), HS-Huffman=(21,52,59,55).
Verify the five phrase-analogy categories and examples in the 3,218-example phrase analogy test set. The table caption states a best-model accuracy of 72%.
targets.notes: The 72% best model is specified later in the body as the ~33B-word, 1000d, HS, full-sentence-context model.

targets.description: Reproduce phrase analogy accuracies for ~1B-word phrase corpus, 300d, context size 5. No-subsampling / 1e-5-subsampling: NEG-5=24/27, NEG-15=27/42, HS-Huffman=19/47.
Reproduce the nearest-entity comparison for infrequent short phrases under NEG-15+1e-5 subsampling versus HS+1e-5 subsampling.

Reproduce additive compositionality examples by element-wise vector addition, reporting the four nearest tokens for examples such as Czech+currency, Vietnam+capital, German+airlines, Russian+river, and French+actress.
Reproduce the large-corpus phrase analogy result: ~33B training words, hierarchical softmax, 1000 dimensions, whole-sentence context -> 72% accuracy; reducing training data to 6B -> 66%.
Reproduce/compare nearest tokens for rare words across published vectors and the large Skip-Phrase model. The Skip-Phrase row is 1000d, about one day training time, and trained on over 30B words.
targets.notes: External published-vector rows are reference baselines, not necessarily retrained.

resources.description: Secondary syntactic relationship evaluation used in W2V1 Table 3.
resources.notes: Distinct from the MSR Sentence Completion Challenge.

resources.name: Microsoft Research Sentence Completion Challenge
resources.description: W2V1 Table-7 resource. The benchmark has 1,040 sentence-completion questions; W2V1 states that its Skip-gram model is trained on 50M words provided with/reference [32].

resources.name: questions-words.txt
resources.description: Original word analogy evaluation set used by W2V1 and W2V2; 19,544 analogy questions in W2V1's count (8,869 semantic + 10,675 syntactic).

resources.name: Internal Google news dataset (~1B words)
resources.description: Original W2V2 word and initial phrase experiments. Words with count <5 are discarded, yielding a 692K vocabulary for the word experiments.

resources.name: W2V2 large phrase training corpus (~33B words)
resources.description: Original large-corpus phrase experiment; the paper only identifies the size (~33B) and compares a 6B reduction. The exact corpus identity/composition is not specified.

resources.name: questions-phrases.txt

resources.description: Public surrogate corpus condition. Current project scope uses the training partition only (829,250,940 words in the previously cataloged count) and excludes held-out data.

resources.name: English Wikipedia 2012 dump

resources.name: Common Crawl 2009-2012
